title: Sensors, Controllers, Alarms, Calibration & Data Quality
level: Environmental, Irrigation & Fertigation Systems Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Cultivation personnel responsible for sensor verification, alarm interpretation, controller-response checks and data-quality escalation
prerequisites: Plant-Environment Measurement & Crop Response and HVAC/Dehumidification/Airflow concepts or equivalent foundation
evidencePolicy: Course uses governed sensor/data-quality, data-integrity and environmental evidence. Calibration/verification concepts are taught as measurement-quality controls; exact calibration methods, tolerances and protected servicing remain instrument- and facility-specific.
assessmentPolicy: Development-only until technical/assessment review, accessibility review and pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize protected calibration, energized electrical servicing, controller-program changes or bypassing alarms/interlocks.
description: Develops specialist sensor and controls reasoning across placement, verification, calibration status, drift, data gaps, alarm logic, command-versus-response, redundancy and evidence-based maintenance handoff.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate sensor representativeness and measurement quality using placement, shielding, verification history, colocated comparison and time-series behavior.
Distinguish verification, calibration, adjustment and protected servicing, and use only suitable verified references for measurement-quality decisions.
Interpret controller commands, alarms, interlocks and physical response as separate evidence layers rather than treating displayed status as proof of delivery.
Analyze missing, flat-lined, intermittent and contradictory data while preserving the original record and explicitly representing uncertainty.
Produce a maintenance/controls handoff that identifies device, time, command, observed response, affected process, verification already completed and safe authority boundary.
